## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1217
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1217
- **Title**: gh-1207 JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1207` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +205
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:01:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:58:05Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Multi-file JS apps now boot: `JsAppEngine` assembles the entry file through the js_widget_runtime assembler (`WidgetManifest.readJs`) instead of eval'ing the raw entry text, so an entry like fa-craft's `import './game/main.js';` renders instead of dying on a bare-import syntax error and spinning forever. Also bumps `js_widget_runtime` `^0.4.121` → `^0.4.153`.

### Key decisions
- Reused the runtime's built-in assembler (`WidgetManifest.fromStorage` + `readJs`): manifest `files` order, relative `import` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped) and `jsr.include()` expansion come for free — no second assembler to maintain.
- New private `_AppWidgetFileReader` bridges env → assembler; it redirects the manifest-namespace entry path (`<dir>/widget.js`) to the engine's real `entryFile`, so live-tile entries assemble their own imports while `manifest.json`, `files` entries and import targets map 1:1 (paths relative to `app.dir`, `dirOverride` respected).
- A missing entry file now throws a clear `StateError` — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw `FileError` from `getOrThrow`).
- The upstream jsr_widget CLI gap (`_loadDirWidget` reads `widget.js` verbatim, still in 0.4.153) is NOT fixable here: `fa jsr widget:test` deliberately delegates to the package's own CLI (invariant I1 in `lib/src/cli/jsr_cli.dart`, zero widget logic in the harness). Needs an upstream `js_widget_runtime` fix; headless `jsr_widget test` still reports `renderCount: 0` for import-based widgets.
- Runtime bump ≥ 0.4.127 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`) fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — mobile gets the native software voxel path instead of the legacy scene3d fallback.

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart --plain-name "multi-file app boot"
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps   # full apps surface (479 tests)
```
Engine-backed tests skip on hosts without the native JS bridge (existing guard); on-device: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → renders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  START[JsAppEngine._start] --> ASM[_assembleEntryJs]
  ASM --> M[WidgetManifest.fromStorage app.dir]
  ASM --> R[_AppWidgetFileReader env]
  R -->|entry path redirect| ENV[ExecutionEnv.readTextFile]
  M --> RJ[WidgetManifest.readJs]
  RJ -->|inline imports + jsr.include, strip export| JS[assembled JS]
  JS --> RUN[JsWidgetEngine.run]
  RUN --> TREE[jsr.render tree — spinner replaced]
```

</details>

# gh-1207: JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner

## Description

## Symptom

Installing **fa-craft** from the fa_widgets catalog on mobile shows a loading spinner forever — the app never renders.

## Root cause

`flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` (`_start`, ~line 330) boots an app by reading only the entry file verbatim:

```dart
final js = (await env.readTextFile('${app.dir}/$entryFile')).getOrThrow();
```

fa-craft's `widget.js` is a one-line multi-file entry:

```js
import './game/main.js';
```

A bare `import` statement is a syntax error in the script-eval engine path, so the JS never executes → no `jsr.render` → `js_app_view.dart` keeps showing `CircularProgressIndicator` (tree stays null).

Note the asymmetry: the **install** side (`catalog_service.dart`) happily unpacks the whole zip (`manifest.json`, `widget.js`, `game/*.js`) into `apps/<id>/` — all files are on disk — but the **boot** side reads just `widget.js` without assembling it. The jsr_widget CLI (`js_widget_runtime/tool/jsr_widget_harness.dart` via `jsr_widget_tool_core.dart` ~line 415) has the same single-file blind spot, so `dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <dir>` also reports `renderCount: 0` for fa-craft while single-file widgets boot fine.

## Fix

Use the runtime's built-in assembler — `WidgetManifest.readJs({required WidgetFileReader reader})` (`js_widget_runtime/lib/src/model/widget_manifest.dart`) already does everything: manifest `files` list, relative `import './x.js'` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped), and `jsr.include()` expansion.

1. In `js_app_engine.dart`, replace the raw `readTextFile(entry)` with a `WidgetManifest` load over a small `WidgetFileReader` adapter backed by `env.readTextFile` (paths relative to `app.dir`). Respect `manifest.widget.entry` when present instead of hardcoding `widget.js`.
2. While here: bump `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `js_widget_runtime` from `^0.4.121` to the latest (^0.4.15x). fa-craft 0.2.x probes for the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, runtime >= 0.4.127) and falls back to the legacy scene3d path on older runtimes — the bump gets mobile the native software voxel path (much faster, and it's the path all fa-craft field testing uses).
3. Regression test: an app folder with `widget.js` = `import './game/main.js';` must boot and render (mirror the existing jsr_widget CLI gap — ideally fix the CLI to use the same assembler so headless `jsr_widget test` covers multi-file widgets too).

## Repro

```sh
# CLI (js_widget_runtime repo) — renderCount: 0, console empty:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <fa-craft dir> --json
# vs single-file widget:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test example/widgets/calculator --json  # renderCount: 1
```

In the app: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → spinner, no error card.

Refs: fa-craft 0.2.18 pinned in IstiN/fa_widgets catalog at `IstiN/fa_craft@204b422`.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1217
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1217
- **Title**: gh-1207 JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1207` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +205
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:01:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:58:05Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Multi-file JS apps now boot: `JsAppEngine` assembles the entry file through the js_widget_runtime assembler (`WidgetManifest.readJs`) instead of eval'ing the raw entry text, so an entry like fa-craft's `import './game/main.js';` renders instead of dying on a bare-import syntax error and spinning forever. Also bumps `js_widget_runtime` `^0.4.121` → `^0.4.153`.

### Key decisions
- Reused the runtime's built-in assembler (`WidgetManifest.fromStorage` + `readJs`): manifest `files` order, relative `import` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped) and `jsr.include()` expansion come for free — no second assembler to maintain.
- New private `_AppWidgetFileReader` bridges env → assembler; it redirects the manifest-namespace entry path (`<dir>/widget.js`) to the engine's real `entryFile`, so live-tile entries assemble their own imports while `manifest.json`, `files` entries and import targets map 1:1 (paths relative to `app.dir`, `dirOverride` respected).
- A missing entry file now throws a clear `StateError` — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw `FileError` from `getOrThrow`).

cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps   # full apps surface (479 tests)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  START[JsAppEngine._start] --> ASM[_assembleEntryJs]
  ASM --> M[WidgetManifest.fromStorage app.dir]
  ASM --> R[_AppWidgetFileReader env]
  R -->|entry path redirect| ENV[ExecutionEnv.readTextFile]

  RJ -->|inline imports + jsr.include, strip export| JS[assembled JS]

# gh-1207: JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner

## Description

## Symptom

Installing **fa-craft** from the fa_widgets catalog on mobile shows a loading spinner forever — the app never renders.

## Root cause

`flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` (`_start`, ~line 330) boots an app by reading only the entry file verbatim:

```dart
final js = (await env.readTextFile('${app.dir}/$entryFile')).getOrThrow();
```

fa-craft's `widget.js` is a one-line multi-file entry:

```js
import './game/main.js';
```

A bare `import` statement is a syntax error in the script-eval engine path, so the JS never executes → no `jsr.render` → `js_app_view.dart` keeps showing `CircularProgressIndicator` (tree stays null).

Note the asymmetry: the **install** side (`catalog_service.dart`) happily unpacks the whole zip (`manifest.json`, `widget.js`, `game/*.js`) into `apps/<id>/` — all files are on disk — but the **boot** side reads just `widget.js` without assembling it. The jsr_widget CLI (`js_widget_runtime/tool/jsr_widget_harness.dart` via `jsr_widget_tool_core.dart` ~line 415) has the same single-file blind spot, so `dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <dir>` also reports `renderCount: 0` for fa-craft while single-file widgets boot fine.

## Fix

Use the runtime's built-in assembler — `WidgetManifest.readJs({required WidgetFileReader reader})` (`js_widget_runtime/lib/src/model/widget_manifest.dart`) already does everything: manifest `files` list, relative `import './x.js'` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped), and `jsr.include()` expansion.

1. In `js_app_engine.dart`, replace the raw `readTextFile(entry)` with a `WidgetManifest` load over a small `WidgetFileReader` adapter backed by `env.readTextFile` (paths relative to `app.dir`). Respect `manifest.widget.entry` when present instead of hardcoding `widget.js`.
2. While here: bump `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `js_widget_runtime` from `^0.4.121` to the latest (^0.4.15x). fa-craft 0.2.x probes for the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, runtime >= 0.4.127) and falls back to the legacy scene3d path on older runtimes — the bump gets mobile the native software voxel path (much faster, and it's the path all fa-craft field testing uses).
3. Regression test: an app folder with `widget.js` = `import './game/main.js';` must boot and render (mirror the existing jsr_widget CLI gap — ideally fix the CLI to use the same assembler so headless `jsr_widget test` covers multi-file widgets too).

## Repro

```sh
# CLI (js_widget_runtime repo) — renderCount: 0, console empty:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <fa-craft dir> --json
# vs single-file widget:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test example/widgets/calculator --json  # renderCount: 1
```

In the app: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → spinner, no error card.

Refs: fa-craft 0.2.18 pinned in IstiN/fa_widgets catalog at `IstiN/fa_craft@204b422`.

1. **The `_AppWidgetFileReader` placement bug**: Look at the diff closely!

```dart

Look at the doc comment: "Host-side engine for one JS app: owns the [JsWidgetEngine], wires every `jsr.*` I/O call... durable fields plus a `rev`/`writer` guard so sibling engines adopt external changes instead of fighting over them." — that's the doc for `JsAppEngine`. The new `_AppWidgetFileReader` class is inserted between the JsAppEngine doc comment and the `JsAppEngine` class declaration, which **detaches the doc comment from `JsAppEngine`**. In Dart, a doc comment must be immediately followed by the declaration it documents. Now `/// Host-side engine for one JS app: ...` doc comment... wait, actually let me re-check.

In Dart, a doc comment attached to nothing is actually analyzer hint? Let me think. A `///` comment must precede a declaration; if it's followed by a blank line and then another `///` comment then a declaration... The first `///` block would be "dangling documentation comment" — the analyzer has a lint `dangling_library_doc_comments` (which is about library-level doc comments not attached to a directive/declaration). Yes! `dangling_library_doc_comments` lint: "docs attached to nothing at the top of a file". That lint applies to doc comments at the start of a library. Here it's in the middle of the file. Hmm, the lint `dangling_library_doc_comments` only applies to comments before the first declaration? Actually it applies anywhere a doc comment is not attached to any declaration... Actually more importantly: the doc comment for `_AppWidgetFileReader` is fine, but the long doc comment for JsAppEngine is now orphaned — the `class JsAppEngine` no longer has its documentation attached (the doc comment is separated from the class by the entire `_AppWidgetFileReader` class). 2. **`exists()` implementation uses `readTextFile`**: `exists` reads the whole file content just to check existence. For the manifest entry check (`WidgetManifest.fromStorage` calls `reader.exists('$dir/widget.js')`), the reader redirects `'$dir/widget.js'` to `'$dir/$entryFile'`, reads the whole entry file — fine, it's needed anyway. But `exists` reading entire file content could be wasteful for large files; acceptable though since content is read anyway. Minor.

But wait — there's a subtle behavioral change: previously, when the entry file was missing, `env.readTextFile(...)` returned a `FileError` result and `getOrThrow()` threw that error. The PR description says "A missing entry file now throws a clear StateError — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw FileError from getOrThrow)". That's the intent. OK.

3. **What about `manifest.json` presence changing boot behavior**: `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` reads `manifest.json` if present and parses `files`. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1217
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1217
- **Title**: gh-1207 JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1207` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +205
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:01:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:58:05Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Multi-file JS apps now boot: `JsAppEngine` assembles the entry file through the js_widget_runtime assembler (`WidgetManifest.readJs`) instead of eval'ing the raw entry text, so an entry like fa-craft's `import './game/main.js';` renders instead of dying on a bare-import syntax error and spinning forever. Also bumps `js_widget_runtime` `^0.4.121` → `^0.4.153`.

### Key decisions
- Reused the runtime's built-in assembler (`WidgetManifest.fromStorage` + `readJs`): manifest `files` order, relative `import` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped) and `jsr.include()` expansion come for free — no second assembler to maintain.
- New private `_AppWidgetFileReader` bridges env → assembler; it redirects the manifest-namespace entry path (`<dir>/widget.js`) to the engine's real `entryFile`, so live-tile entries assemble their own imports while `manifest.json`, `files` entries and import targets map 1:1 (paths relative to `app.dir`, `dirOverride` respected).
- A missing entry file now throws a clear `StateError` — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw `FileError` from `getOrThrow`).
- The upstream jsr_widget CLI gap (`_loadDirWidget` reads `widget.js` verbatim, still in 0.4.153) is NOT fixable here: `fa jsr widget:test` deliberately delegates to the package's own CLI (invariant I1 in `lib/src/cli/jsr_cli.dart`, zero widget logic in the harness). Needs an upstream `js_widget_runtime` fix; headless `jsr_widget test` still reports `renderCount: 0` for import-based widgets.
- Runtime bump ≥ 0.4.127 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`) fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — mobile gets the native software voxel path instead of the legacy scene3d fallback.

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart --plain-name "multi-file app boot"
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps   # full apps surface (479 tests)
```
Engine-backed tests skip on hosts without the native JS bridge (existing guard); on-device: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → renders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  START[JsAppEngine._start] --> ASM[_assembleEntryJs]
  ASM --> M[WidgetManifest.fromStorage app.dir]
  ASM --> R[_AppWidgetFileReader env]
  R -->|entry path redirect| ENV[ExecutionEnv.readTextFile]
  M --> RJ[WidgetManifest.readJs]
  RJ -->|inline imports + jsr.include, strip export| JS[assembled JS]
  JS --> RUN[JsWidgetEngine.run]
  RUN --> TREE[jsr.render tree — spinner replaced]
```

</details>

# gh-1207: JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner

## Description

## Symptom

Installing **fa-craft** from the fa_widgets catalog on mobile shows a loading spinner forever — the app never renders.

## Root cause

`flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` (`_start`, ~line 330) boots an app by reading only the entry file verbatim:

```dart
final js = (await env.readTextFile('${app.dir}/$entryFile')).getOrThrow();
```

fa-craft's `widget.js` is a one-line multi-file entry:

```js
import './game/main.js';
```

A bare `import` statement is a syntax error in the script-eval engine path, so the JS never executes → no `jsr.render` → `js_app_view.dart` keeps showing `CircularProgressIndicator` (tree stays null).

Note the asymmetry: the **install** side (`catalog_service.dart`) happily unpacks the whole zip (`manifest.json`, `widget.js`, `game/*.js`) into `apps/<id>/` — all files are on disk — but the **boot** side reads just `widget.js` without assembling it. The jsr_widget CLI (`js_widget_runtime/tool/jsr_widget_harness.dart` via `jsr_widget_tool_core.dart` ~line 415) has the same single-file blind spot, so `dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <dir>` also reports `renderCount: 0` for fa-craft while single-file widgets boot fine.

## Fix

Use the runtime's built-in assembler — `WidgetManifest.readJs({required WidgetFileReader reader})` (`js_widget_runtime/lib/src/model/widget_manifest.dart`) already does everything: manifest `files` list, relative `import './x.js'` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped), and `jsr.include()` expansion.

1. In `js_app_engine.dart`, replace the raw `readTextFile(entry)` with a `WidgetManifest` load over a small `WidgetFileReader` adapter backed by `env.readTextFile` (paths relative to `app.dir`). Respect `manifest.widget.entry` when present instead of hardcoding `widget.js`.
2. While here: bump `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `js_widget_runtime` from `^0.4.121` to the latest (^0.4.15x). fa-craft 0.2.x probes for the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, runtime >= 0.4.127) and falls back to the legacy scene3d path on older runtimes — the bump gets mobile the native software voxel path (much faster, and it's the path all fa-craft field testing uses).
3. Regression test: an app folder with `widget.js` = `import './game/main.js';` must boot and render (mirror the existing jsr_widget CLI gap — ideally fix the CLI to use the same assembler so headless `jsr_widget test` covers multi-file widgets too).

## Repro

```sh
# CLI (js_widget_runtime repo) — renderCount: 0, console empty:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <fa-craft dir> --json
# vs single-file widget:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test example/widgets/calculator --json  # renderCount: 1
```

In the app: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → spinner, no error card.

Refs: fa-craft 0.2.18 pinned in IstiN/fa_widgets catalog at `IstiN/fa_craft@204b422`.

0.4.153 exists on pub.dev (published 2026-10-03, one day before the PR). The pubspec bump `^0.4.121` → `^0.4.153` forces the floor.

Now, key review areas:

1. **The `_AppWidgetFileReader` placement bug**: Look at the diff closely!

```dart
/// storage key (protocol: docs in `fa_widgets/docs/state-sync.md`) —
/// durable fields plus a `rev`/`writer` guard so sibling engines adopt
/// external changes instead of fighting over them.
+
+/// [WidgetFileReader] over the app's [ExecutionEnv] behind
...
+class _AppWidgetFileReader implements WidgetFileReader {
...
+}
+
 class JsAppEngine {
```

The class was inserted between the class doc comment of `JsAppEngine` and the `class JsAppEngine` declaration! Look at the doc comment: "Host-side engine for one JS app: owns the [JsWidgetEngine], wires every `jsr.*` I/O call... durable fields plus a `rev`/`writer` guard so sibling engines adopt external changes instead of fighting over them." — that's the doc for `JsAppEngine`. The new `_AppWidgetFileReader` class is inserted between the JsAppEngine doc comment and the `JsAppEngine` class declaration, which **detaches the doc comment from `JsAppEngine`**. In Dart, a doc comment must be immediately followed by the declaration it documents. Now `/// Host-side engine for one JS app: ...` doc comment... wait, actually let me re-check.

In the diff:
```
 /// storage key (protocol: docs in `fa_widgets/docs/state-sync.md`) —
 /// durable fields plus a `rev`/`writer` guard so sibling engines adopt
 /// external changes instead of fighting over them.
+
+/// [WidgetFileReader] over the app's [ExecutionEnv] behind
...
+}
+
 class JsAppEngine {
```

So the big doc comment for JsAppEngine ("Host-side engine for one JS app...") now dangles: it's followed by a blank line and then the `_AppWidgetFileReader` doc comment. Actually wait — the doc comment ends with "external changes instead of fighting over them." then a blank line, then `/// [WidgetFileReader] over...` doc for `_AppWidgetFileReader`, then the class, then `class JsAppEngine`.

Since there's a blank line between the JsAppEngine doc comment and the `_AppWidgetFileReader` doc comment, dartdoc attaches `/// Host-side engine for one JS app...` to... nothing? In Dart, a doc comment attached to nothing is actually analyzer hint? Let me think. A `///` comment must precede a declaration; if it's followed by a blank line and then another `///` comment then a declaration... The first `///` block would be "dangling documentation comment" — the analyzer has a lint `dangling_library_doc_comments` (which is about library-level doc comments not attached to a directive/declaration). Yes! `dangling_library_doc_comments` lint: "docs attached to nothing at the top of a file". That lint applies to doc comments at the start of a library. Here it's in the middle of the file. Hmm, the lint `dangling_library_doc_comments` only applies to comments before the first declaration? Actually it applies anywhere a doc comment is not attached to any declaration... Let me check analysis_options.yaml.

Actually more importantly: the doc comment for `_AppWidgetFileReader` is fine, but the long doc comment for JsAppEngine is now orphaned — the `class JsAppEngine` no longer has its documentation attached (the doc comment is separated from the class by the entire `_AppWidgetFileReader` class). This means dartdoc/docs tools would attach that big doc to nothing. This is a real code-quality issue: the class doc should have been moved with the class or the reader class placed after JsAppEngine. Severity: IMPORTANT (docs detach; possibly analyzer warning).

Let me check analysis_options.yaml to see if dangling_library_doc_comments is enabled. Even if not, it's still a code-organization issue.

2. **`exists()` implementation uses `readTextFile`**: `exists` reads the whole file content just to check existence. For the manifest entry check (`WidgetManifest.fromStorage` calls `reader.exists('$dir/widget.js')`), the reader redirects `'$dir/widget.js'` to `'$dir/$entryFile'`, reads the whole entry file — fine, it's needed anyway. But `exists` reading entire file content could be wasteful for large files; acceptable though since content is read anyway. Minor.

But wait — there's a subtle behavioral change: previously, when the entry file was missing, `env.readTextFile(...)` returned a `FileError` result and `getOrThrow()` threw that error. The PR description says "A missing entry file now throws a clear StateError — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw FileError from getOrThrow)". That's the intent. OK.

3. **What about `manifest.json` presence changing boot behavior**: `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` reads `manifest.json` if present and parses `files`. Previously the engine ignored `manifest.json`'s `files` list entirely and just eval'd the entry file. Now, if an app has a `manifest.json` with a `files` list, the boot path concatenates the files listed **instead of** reading the entry file! Look at `readJs`: if `files != null && files.isNotEmpty`, it reads each file in `files` — the `widget.js` entry (redirected to `entryFile`) is NOT read at all. This is a behavioral change for existing single-file apps that have a manifest.json with a `files` list: previously they'd boot the entry file verbatim; now they boot the concatenation of `files`. Is that a problem? If an app's manifest declares `files`, previously the harness ignored it and booted the entry — if the entry file contained everything (some apps might have been built that way?), the boot would now change behavior. Hmm. But this aligns boot with install/CLI semantics. Also note the second test explicitly covers "manifest files list concatenates the declared order" with `widget.js` = '/* unused: files win */'. So this is deliberate. But is it backward-compatible? An app previously booting fine with an entry file + a manifest.json that happens to contain a `files` list would now boot differently. This is a real backward-compat consideration worth flagging (IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION). Hmm... Actually wait, there's something even more subtle: `files` entries that don't exist produce `/* jsr.include: file not found: $filename */` comment parts — silent. OK.

Another subtlety in `fromStorage`: manifest `id` is derived from `_lastSegment(normalized)` — the app dir name. Not used by the engine (the engine uses app.id from its own manifest). Fine.

4. **The `_map` redirect only handles the exact entry path `$dir/widget.js`**. What if `entryFile` is in a subdirectory? E.g., a live-tile entry `widget_tile.js` in `app.dir` root — fine. What if entryFile is `tiles/main.js`? Then redirect works too ('$dir/widget.js' → '$dir/tiles/main.js'). And relative imports in that entry resolve relative to `tiles/` — via `appDir`... wait, `appDir` returns `widgetPath` = `app.dir` (not single-file). `_resolvePath(baseDir=appDir, relPath)` — for imports inside the entry file content, baseDir is `appDir` (app root), NOT the entry file's directory. So an import `import './game/main.js'` inside `tiles/main.js` would resolve to `apps/<id>/game/main.js`, not `apps/<id>/tiles/game/main.js`. Hmm, but that's upstream assembler behavior (`_preprocessIncludes(js, appDir, ...)` always uses appDir as the base). This matches the CLI behavior presumably. Since inlined imports are resolved relative to appDir always (not the importing file's dir!), wait no — look closer:

```dart
return _preprocessIncludes(
  stripped,
  _parentOf(absPath),
  depth + 1,
  reader,
  visited,
);
```

The nested preprocess uses `_parentOf(absPath)` as baseDir, so imports within imported files resolve relative to the imported file's directory. Only the TOP-level entry's imports resolve relative to `appDir`. Since the entry is (normally) at app root `widget.js`, appDir == entry dir — consistent. With the redirect, the entry content comes from `$dir/$entryFile` (e.g. `widget_tile.js` at app root) — same dir. So OK for root-level entries. An entryFile in a subdir would resolve its imports relative to app root, which could be wrong, but that's an edge case; the assembler has notion of the real entry path. Fine — maybe worth a SUGGE…

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt
## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release commits from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 ruleset-
  bypass App pushes the bump straight to protected main, so the App identity
  is what auditability hangs on.
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` auto-releases a patch to pub.dev
  (`scripts/auto_release.sh` via `ci.yml`) — intended. The version scheme is
  `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a
  monotonic `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again); the core and app pubspecs bump in lockstep.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot
  crash before the first frame white-screens TestFlight with a green gate
  (issue #544: build 160, boot refactor created the platform env before
  `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized`); boot stage order is pinned by
  `flutter_app/test/boot/app_boot_test.dart`.
- TestFlight external distribution (issue #239): the `submit_only` lanes
  (driven by build-mobile.yml / build-macos.yml) distribute every build
  straight to the EXTERNAL group — REQUIRED repo variables
  `TESTFLIGHT_EXTERNAL_GROUP`, `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL`,
  `BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_PHONE`, `BETA_APP_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` (lanes fail loudly
  at start without them). Pilot must WAIT for processing (skipping the wait
  silently skips distribution); `verify_external_distribution!` asserts
  group membership bounded — beta-review-pending is a neutral notice, a
  build never reaching the group fails the leg (self-filed issue).
- Manual App Store review: `release-appstore.yml` (workflow_dispatch:
  `version` + `platforms` ios/macos/both + `confirm` repeating the version)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1217
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1217
- **Title**: gh-1207 JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1207` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +205
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T06:01:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T06:58:05Z

## PR Description

### What changed
Multi-file JS apps now boot: `JsAppEngine` assembles the entry file through the js_widget_runtime assembler (`WidgetManifest.readJs`) instead of eval'ing the raw entry text, so an entry like fa-craft's `import './game/main.js';` renders instead of dying on a bare-import syntax error and spinning forever. Also bumps `js_widget_runtime` `^0.4.121` → `^0.4.153`.

### Key decisions
- Reused the runtime's built-in assembler (`WidgetManifest.fromStorage` + `readJs`): manifest `files` order, relative `import` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped) and `jsr.include()` expansion come for free — no second assembler to maintain.
- New private `_AppWidgetFileReader` bridges env → assembler; it redirects the manifest-namespace entry path (`<dir>/widget.js`) to the engine's real `entryFile`, so live-tile entries assemble their own imports while `manifest.json`, `files` entries and import targets map 1:1 (paths relative to `app.dir`, `dirOverride` respected).
- A missing entry file now throws a clear `StateError` — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw `FileError` from `getOrThrow`).
- The upstream jsr_widget CLI gap (`_loadDirWidget` reads `widget.js` verbatim, still in 0.4.153) is NOT fixable here: `fa jsr widget:test` deliberately delegates to the package's own CLI (invariant I1 in `lib/src/cli/jsr_cli.dart`, zero widget logic in the harness). Needs an upstream `js_widget_runtime` fix; headless `jsr_widget test` still reports `renderCount: 0` for import-based widgets.
- Runtime bump ≥ 0.4.127 ships the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`) fa-craft 0.2.x probes for — mobile gets the native software voxel path instead of the legacy scene3d fallback.

### How to verify
```bash
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/js_app_engine_test.dart --plain-name "multi-file app boot"
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps   # full apps surface (479 tests)
```
Engine-backed tests skip on hosts without the native JS bridge (existing guard); on-device: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → renders.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  START[JsAppEngine._start] --> ASM[_assembleEntryJs]
  ASM --> M[WidgetManifest.fromStorage app.dir]
  ASM --> R[_AppWidgetFileReader env]
  R -->|entry path redirect| ENV[ExecutionEnv.readTextFile]
  M --> RJ[WidgetManifest.readJs]
  RJ -->|inline imports + jsr.include, strip export| JS[assembled JS]
  JS --> RUN[JsWidgetEngine.run]
  RUN --> TREE[jsr.render tree — spinner replaced]
```

</details>

# gh-1207: JS app engine doesn't assemble multi-file widgets — fa-craft (and any import-based app) boots to an eternal spinner

## Description

## Symptom

Installing **fa-craft** from the fa_widgets catalog on mobile shows a loading spinner forever — the app never renders.

## Root cause

`flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart` (`_start`, ~line 330) boots an app by reading only the entry file verbatim:

```dart
final js = (await env.readTextFile('${app.dir}/$entryFile')).getOrThrow();
```

fa-craft's `widget.js` is a one-line multi-file entry:

```js
import './game/main.js';
```

A bare `import` statement is a syntax error in the script-eval engine path, so the JS never executes → no `jsr.render` → `js_app_view.dart` keeps showing `CircularProgressIndicator` (tree stays null).

Note the asymmetry: the **install** side (`catalog_service.dart`) happily unpacks the whole zip (`manifest.json`, `widget.js`, `game/*.js`) into `apps/<id>/` — all files are on disk — but the **boot** side reads just `widget.js` without assembling it. The jsr_widget CLI (`js_widget_runtime/tool/jsr_widget_harness.dart` via `jsr_widget_tool_core.dart` ~line 415) has the same single-file blind spot, so `dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <dir>` also reports `renderCount: 0` for fa-craft while single-file widgets boot fine.

## Fix

Use the runtime's built-in assembler — `WidgetManifest.readJs({required WidgetFileReader reader})` (`js_widget_runtime/lib/src/model/widget_manifest.dart`) already does everything: manifest `files` list, relative `import './x.js'` inlining (depth-capped, each file once, `export` stripped), and `jsr.include()` expansion.

1. In `js_app_engine.dart`, replace the raw `readTextFile(entry)` with a `WidgetManifest` load over a small `WidgetFileReader` adapter backed by `env.readTextFile` (paths relative to `app.dir`). Respect `manifest.widget.entry` when present instead of hardcoding `widget.js`.
2. While here: bump `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` `js_widget_runtime` from `^0.4.121` to the latest (^0.4.15x). fa-craft 0.2.x probes for the bridge-side voxel renderer (`voxel.attach`, runtime >= 0.4.127) and falls back to the legacy scene3d path on older runtimes — the bump gets mobile the native software voxel path (much faster, and it's the path all fa-craft field testing uses).
3. Regression test: an app folder with `widget.js` = `import './game/main.js';` must boot and render (mirror the existing jsr_widget CLI gap — ideally fix the CLI to use the same assembler so headless `jsr_widget test` covers multi-file widgets too).

## Repro

```sh
# CLI (js_widget_runtime repo) — renderCount: 0, console empty:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test <fa-craft dir> --json
# vs single-file widget:
dart run bin/jsr_widget.dart test example/widgets/calculator --json  # renderCount: 1
```

In the app: install Fa Craft from the catalog → open → spinner, no error card.

Refs: fa-craft 0.2.18 pinned in IstiN/fa_widgets catalog at `IstiN/fa_craft@204b422`.

But wait — there's a subtle behavioral change: previously, when the entry file was missing, `env.readTextFile(...)` returned a `FileError` result and `getOrThrow()` threw that error. The PR description says "A missing entry file now throws a clear StateError — the view shows its error card instead of an eternal spinner (previously a raw FileError from getOrThrow)". That's the intent. OK.

3. **What about `manifest.json` presence changing boot behavior**: `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` reads `manifest.json` if present and parses `files`. Previously the engine ignored `manifest.json`'s `files` list entirely and just eval'd the entry file. Now, if an app has a `manifest.json` with a `files` list, the boot path concatenates the files listed **instead of** reading the entry file! Look at `readJs`: if `files != null && files.isNotEmpty`, it reads each file in `files` — the `widget.js` entry (redirected to `entryFile`) is NOT read at all. This is a behavioral change for existing single-file apps that have a manifest.json with a `files` list: previously they'd boot the entry file verbatim; now they boot the concatenation of `files`. Is that a problem? If an app's manifest declares `files`, previously the harness ignored it and booted the entry — if the entry file contained everything (some apps might have been built that way?), the boot would now change behavior. Hmm. But this aligns boot with install/CLI semantics. Also note the second test explicitly covers "manifest files list concatenates the declared order" with `widget.js` = '/* unused: files win */'. Another subtlety in `fromStorage`: manifest `id` is derived from `_lastSegment(normalized)` — the app dir name. Not used by the engine (the engine uses app.id from its own manifest). Fine.

So an import `import './game/main.js'` inside `tiles/main.js` would resolve to `apps/<id>/game/main.js`, not `apps/<id>/tiles/game/main.js`. Hmm, but that's upstream assembler behavior (`_preprocessIncludes(js, appDir, ...)` always uses appDir as the base). This matches the CLI behavior presumably. Since inlined imports are resolved relative to appDir always (not the importing file's dir!), wait no — look closer:

return _preprocessIncludes(

With the redirect, the entry content comes from `$dir/$entryFile` (e.g. `widget_tile.js` at app root) — same dir. So OK for root-level entries. **A. `WidgetManifest.fromStorage` uses `_lastSegment(app.dir)` for id etc. — not relevant to the engine.**

**B. Manifest `files` list behavior change (backward compat):** If an installed app has `manifest.json` WITH a `files` list, `readJs` reads the `files` in order and the entry file (`widget.js` → redirected `entryFile`) is NOT evaluated at all. Before this PR, the engine booted `entryFile` verbatim regardless of `manifest.json`. After: `files` wins. Is any existing installed app affected? Apps are installed from the fa_widgets catalog as zips. If any catalog app ships a `files` list, its boot behavior changes from "entry only" to "concatenated files". For apps designed for the jsr CLI semantics, `files` lists are the load order — concatenation is the CORRECT behavior and entry is normally included in files or is the fallback. But for an app whose manifest.json has a `files` list AND whose widget.js was self-contained (not listing widget.js in files), boot now silently skips the entry. This is a real behavior change worth flagging — but the second test pins it as DESIRED ("files win"). The ticket's fix instructions said "a manifest `files` list defines the load order" is part of the assembler contract, so this is intentional per ticket. I'll note as SUGGESTION (document behavior) or IMPORTANT? Given catalog apps target the jsr runtime semantics and the CLI uses the same assembler, alignment is correct — apps built for the platform should already be consistent. SUGGESTION.

**C. The `_map` redirect only remaps the exact string `'$dir/widget.js'`.** Consider `fromStorage`: `jsPath = '$normalized/widget.js'` where normalized = `_normalizePath(app.dir)`. If app.dir contains backslashes (Windows), normalized would have forward slashes but the reader's `dir` (raw app.dir) might have backslashes → mismatch. On mobile (iOS/Android), forward slashes — fine. Edge case, not worth flagging beyond a nit. Actually `_normalizePath` only replaces `\` with `/`. app.dir comes from apps_store — always forward slashes. Skip.

**D. Redirect + `files` interplay:** if manifest lists `'widget.js'` in `files`, redirect applies — consistent.
